body:
There are a few discrepancies between the two implementations of `PhysicsServer3D::body_test_motion`, which is what indirectly powers `move_and_slide` (and a few other methods), that will cause things like `is_on_floor`, `is_on_ceiling` and `is_on_wall` to behave a bit weird when using Jolt, which is sort of tied to the slide collisions that were last reported, so I suspect this is related to that.

I would need to debug the MRP to verify that this is in fact the cause here, which might be a while before I can get around to doing, as debugging this is time-consuming, but I'm fairly certain of it even without debugging this.

If this is that discrepancy, then it's unfortunately highly unlikely that this will be fixed by me. I've spent quite a bit of time experimenting with different implementations of `body_test_motion`, including what is essentially a straight copy of the Godot Physics one, and I either end up with a prohibitive amount of ghost collisions, or the "sensory" parts of `CharacterBody3D` break down (`is_on_wall`, etc), as seems to be the case here.

EDIT: To be even more specific, this is the code that is likely causing the issue here:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/af2c713971499953373380b9ae8673f64423bd59/modules/jolt_physics/spaces/jolt_physics_direct_space_state_3d.cpp#L342-L348

Basically, if a contact normal is deemed to not obstruct the direction of movement, that contact is discarded.

Removing this code will likely fix the issue here, but will cause a significant amount of ghost collisions in all kinds of circumstances, to the point where `CharacterBody3D` is virtually useless for any sort of general application.
